newsitem.title: UK: Bradys on hold ahead of crucial U.S. ECI data.
newsitem.headline: Bradys on hold ahead of crucial U.S. ECI data.

text.p: There was little for emerging market debt traders to do during the Tuesday morning session in London, as the market waited for the release of U.S. data.
"The market is pretty much unchanged across the board from New York levels," a debt trader at a European bank said.
"We have the ECI at 1230 GMT, which is Alan Greenspan's favourite number. Everybody will be watching that number, and will be the first directional trigger for the rest of the week."
The first quarter U.S. employment cost index (ECI) is predicted to rise by 0.9 percent versus a 0.8 percent increase in the last report, a Reuters poll of U.S. economists said.

The figure will be closely watched for signs of a build-up of inflationary pressures in the U.S., which could lead to an interest rate hike at the next Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on May 20.
Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan will address the International Monetary Fund/World Bank spring meeting in Washington at 1630 GMT.

"Volumes are thin, there is no price action and everyone is waiting to see what will happen this afternoon," a dealer at a U.S. bank said, adding Friday's release of unemployment data for April would also be closely watched.
